Dynasty rating58 / 100
A Balanced archetype fills every role at a sensible price at the auction rather than chasing value or star power. Dynasty rating rebuilds every auction from squad continuity and recent titles — cross 65 and it starts paying: a real fan-sentiment lift and a small on-field culture edge.
Campaign coaching
Head coachYou
Circuit reputationBuilding
ContractReal, multi-year · not a seasonal fee
A domestic-club coach is available for a franchise role in any country — the franchise is the senior relationship, so its campaign window takes priority the moment it opens, whatever else is on the calendar.
Franchise finances
Central pool this campaign18.4cr
Local revenue · fan sentiment4.1cr
Operating costs-6.2cr
Every franchise draws an equal share of a central pool sized to comfortably cover a full auction purse, on top of its own local revenue. A hard reserve floor of 3.0cr applies whatever the season did — a franchise cannot go bankrupt, and it carries no financial fair play exposure the way the domestic club does.
This campaign’s own timeline
Four genuinely separate, separately-dated events — not one sitting. Whichever players the EOI meeting finalises are what the auction actually bids on.
EOI MeetingRegistered-player list finalised into the auction shortlist · held 52 days ago
Pre-Auction MeetingThe room locks in its plan and targets · held 12 days ago
War Room & AuctionRetention, RTM cards and the live bidding room · auction window opens today
Trade CentreThe quarterly trade window · outside the auction cycle
Campaign staff
Held on real, year-round multi-year contracts — the franchise is the senior relationship the moment its own window opens, but a specialist here isn’t re-hired from scratch every campaign the way a fresh coaching fee would imply.

No youth academy and no domestic overseas-quota rules apply here — a franchise really is built differently from the club menu, just not staff-free the way it once looked.
Campaign review
Judged end-of-campaign only — never a mid-season sacking the way a domestic board can move. A title lifts your circuit reputation; a genuinely poor finish can end even a real multi-year deal early, with the replacement appointed immediately so the franchise is never coachless.
Franchise Owner

Training

Preparation week · 4 days until the Lahore Lions fixture
This week
Preparation week — no fixture inside three days, so the programme runs at full intensity. A match week drops development to zero and the whole squad works on recovery and shape instead; the off-season is where a young player genuinely rebuilds his game.
Who decides
Delegated by default — a specialist coach reads a player's genuine weakest cluster on his own. Untick to name a focus yourself for a specific player, from his own profile.

First-Class Championship · between windows
Pakistan's three-format domestic season runs the T20 Cup, the List A Cup and the First-Class Championship on their own separate windows rather than all at once - the Championship's own window opens once the T20 Cup finishes out, so there is honestly nothing scheduled here yet. Islamabad Icons finished 4th in last season's Championship.
What a multi-day match actually carries
Two real mechanics with no honest surface in a T20 fixture: session-by-session AMBITION (both sides genuinely reassess win/draw/loss chances at every break, not just at the toss - a side three hundred behind with four wickets left is surviving; turn the match around and the same reassessment goes for a win) and real time lost to rain, made up for on the following days within the laws (extra time, an earlier start, never past the final day's own arrears) rather than simply vanishing from the match. Both will show up here once the Championship window is actually live.
List A Cup · between windows
The List A Cup sits on its own window later in the year, after the First-Class Championship closes out - nothing to schedule here while the T20 Cup is still the season's live competition. Islamabad Icons reached the semi-final last time it was played.

ShapeBilateral, home series · no fixed cap
PlayerRoleStatus
Preferred squad size
A bilateral series like this carries no fixed cap and allows a mid-series replacement (delayed by rule to the NEXT match, never the one in progress) — a tournament squad works differently: a fixed cap plus named reserves, promoted with no cooling-off. Confirming here never clears the OTHER two formats’ own squads — each is tracked, called up and submitted independently.
Injury · mid-series replacement available
Zain Chaudhry is a doubt for the remainder of this home series. A replacement can be called up now — by rule, he is only eligible from the next match, never the one already in progress.
Selection meeting · genuinely optional
The panel doesn’t always sit for this. A meeting is always held for a side’s first-ever squad in a competition, or whenever turnover is 2 or more players; otherwise it’s a real probability read off the panel’s own thoroughness — and you can switch it off entirely in your own preferences.

Major tournament
340
days to the ICC World T20 Championship · a genuine major (International scope, Prestige 85)
Inside 120 days of a major, the panel holds one extra, genuinely additional pool-shaping meeting — on top of, not instead of, the ordinary annual review. The board also judges you differently once one is played: winning it is worth far more trust than an ordinary bilateral win, and falling short of the board’s own stated target (“reach the final” this cycle) here specifically is read as “his job is on the line,” not just a disappointing week.
Central contracts · the full list, every team
Last announced4 months ago · you drew up the list
Next announcementdue in around 5 months, once the domestic season concludes
The evaluator's own best-format ranking across the whole domestic pool feeds the announcement — but the tier list itself is drawn up by you, not handed down by the board. At the annual announcement you hold full authority: promote, demote, bring in anyone from the domestic pool, or drop a name entirely. Between announcements you can still revisit an already-contracted player's tier or NOC status any time you like — the small “Manage” action on his own row below — but that standing review can never induct someone who wasn't already on the list; a genuine outsider only ever comes in through the next full announcement, or a petition heard in between.

Standing authority · tiers, NOC, and what you can't do here
Grant or deny NOC yourself, any time — it's your call, not the board's, on whether a centrally-contracted player is also released for a clashing franchise season. International duty always wins the clash regardless of what you decide here; NOC denial only ever withholds the franchise release, never the series itself. It's only ever a live question for a Tier A or Tier B contract — Tier C and uncontracted players are never subject to it.
Reassigning a tier or an NOC call from a player's own “Manage” button works whenever you like, all season. What it can't do: bring in a name who isn't already on this list. A genuine outsider only ever joins through the next full announcement — or gets heard, not guaranteed, through a petition in between.

Who are you?

Biographical details
Playing background shapes how a real board reads you early on — it isn’t a shortcut past starting small.
Starting coaching license
LicenseBasic
Every coach starts here, whatever the playing background — there is no shortcut to a higher badge at creation. A license only rises through real tenure and results (Basic → Level 1 → Level 2 → Level 3 → Advanced → International Elite), and a head-coach vacancy at a serious club will simply be closed to you until it does. Many careers genuinely start in a specialist staff seat instead — those carry no license requirement at all.
New Career · Career Setup

Where do you start?

A club job, a franchise, an international post, or find your own way in from unemployed — real, genuinely different jobs, not the same screens under a different badge

Club Manager

A permanent, year-round domestic post — recruitment, a boardroom, a youth academy, a season-long budget.

Franchise Manager

A campaign-bound multi-year post — no academy, no transfer market, a squad built entirely at the auction.

International Manager

No transfer market, no academy — a national pool, a squad drawn from it, and a board that judges you on majors.

Unemployed

Start with nothing and work through the real job market — exactly what an AI coach without a job does every month.

New Career · Job Market

Every real board advert in the world right now, the same list an AI coach applies against
There is no interview here — a real advert simply gathers every eligible applicant and appoints the best fit once its own window closes. Applying is the whole decision on your side; the board’s decision comes later, on its own date.
